subsystems.name: Active small-molecule cocktail
subsystems.role: modulates epigenetic enzymes to reset DNA methylation patterns toward a younger state.

subsystems.name: Topical delivery system
subsystems.role: carries the active molecules through the skin barrier to reach target cells.

subsystems.name: Formulation base
subsystems.role: provides a stable, spreadable vehicle for skin application.

subsystems.name: Epigenetic readout and control
subsystems.role: measures methylation age and ensures reprogramming remains partial, not full pluripotency.

subsystems.name: Safety and toxicology
subsystems.role: detects any risk of cancer, unwanted cell fate changes, or immune reactions.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing and quality control
subsystems.role: produces a consistent, sterile product at scale.
parts: analytical methods for potency and purity

buildSteps.title: Map target methylation sites
buildSteps.detail: Compare methylation patterns in young versus aged skin cells to identify which CpG sites should be reset.

buildSteps.title: Screen small molecules
buildSteps.detail: Test libraries of compounds for their ability to alter methylation in skin cells without driving full pluripotency.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the cocktail
buildSteps.detail: Combine active molecules with penetration enhancers and stabilizers into a topical cream or gel.

buildSteps.title: Test on human skin models
buildSteps.detail: Apply the formulation to 3D skin equivalents or explants, then measure epigenetic age reversal and confirm cells retain their skin identity.

buildSteps.title: Assess safety
buildSteps.detail: Check for oncogenic transformation, teratoma formation, and off-target effects in animal models.

buildSteps.title: Run clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Phase I trials test safety in humans; Phase II trials look for measurable improvement in skin aging signs.

buildSteps.title: Scale up and manufacture
buildSteps.detail: Produce under GMP conditions, with stability and sterility testing for the final topical product.

buildSteps.title: Regulatory approval and launch
buildSteps.detail: If trials succeed, seek approval as a cosmetic or drug, then make it commercially available.

prerequisites.why: they provide a quantitative measure of biological age from DNA methylation, essential for proving any reversal.
demonstrated in mice and cells using gene therapy, but not yet achieved safely in human skin with small molecules.
some compounds can alter methylation, but a safe and effective cocktail for skin remains to be found.

prerequisites.tech: Topical drug delivery to skin cells
prerequisites.why: many small molecules can penetrate the skin, but targeting specific cell types and avoiding systemic exposure is challenging.
the risk of cancer or loss of cell identity from reprogramming must be ruled out before any human use.

pathway.milestone: laboratory research identifying small molecules and testing them on cultured skin cells
pathway.unlocks: a shortlist of candidate compounds and initial evidence of partial epigenetic resetting.

pathway.milestone: preclinical studies on human skin explants and animal safety models
pathway.unlocks: proof that a topical formulation can reverse epigenetic age without harm.

pathway.milestone: first-in-human clinical trials for safety and early efficacy
pathway.unlocks: data on whether the treatment works in people and is well tolerated.

pathway.milestone: approved topical products for skin rejuvenation
pathway.unlocks: a commercially available way to reduce signs of skin aging by resetting epigenetic marks.
